blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Large language models have been widely used to generate plausible research ideas, yet it remains unclear what makes automated ideation effective and how generated novel proposals arise from prior scientific work. We introduce the Creative AI Researcher (CAR), an agentic framework combining literature grounding, iterative development and explicit conceptual operators. CAR constructs a semantic knowledge graph from retrieved literature and equips an ideation agent with graph-retrieval tools and four operators: bisociation, analogy, exploration and elaboration. Each operator call is checked against structural acceptance conditions and recorded, producing a trace of intermediate transformations and declared literature sources. We evaluate CAR with two language-model backbones across 40 LiveIdeaBench research topics and two execution benchmarks. CAR achieves significantly higher methodological novelty (MN) than single-shot prompting and The AI Scientist. Its methodological novelty does not differ significantly from the Research Ideation Agent, while its feasibility scores are higher on both backbones. With a shared experiment executor, CAR achieves the highest pairwise win rate among the evaluated AI methods on FML-bench-Lite and BioXArena. In a ten-condition ablation study, MN point estimates favor CAR over one-step proposal on both backbones, but no MN contrast survives correction for multiple comparisons. The results do not establish a consistent quality benefit from explicit operators beyond free-form iteration. CAR makes the sequence of operations and declared literature sources inspectable, separating judged idea quality from procedural traceability.
blocks.zh: 大型语言模型被广泛用于产生可信的研究想法,但尚不清楚是什么使得自动化想法有效,以及以往科学工作如何产生新的建议。 我们介绍了创意人工智能研究员(CAR),这是一个将文献定位、迭代发展和明确的概念操作者相结合的代理框架。 CAR从检索的文献中构建一个语义知识图,并为一个构思剂配备了图检索工具和四个操作符:类比,类比,探索和阐述. 每个操作员的呼叫都根据结构接受条件进行核对,并记录下来,产生一定的中间转换和申报的文献来源。 我们用两个语言模式的骨干来评价CAR,涉及40个LiveIdea Bench研究课题和两个执行基准。 CAR在方法上的新颖性显著高于单发提示和AI科学家。 它在方法上的新颖性与"研究思想代理人"(Research Ideation Agent)没有显著的区别,而其可行性分数在两种骨干上都较高. 通过共享实验执行器,CAR在FML-bench-Lite和BioXArena上获得评价的AI方法中实现了最高的对偶胜率. 在10个条件的减肥研究中,MN点估计对CAR优于两根骨干上的单步建议,但MN对比无法幸存的多次比较修正. 其结果不能证明明确操作者在自由形式迭代之外具有一致的质量效益。 CAR使行动序列和申报的文献来源可以检查,将判断的思想质量与程序的可追踪性分开。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
AI scientists, LLM agents that propose research ideas, implement them and report the results, have moved from demonstrations to systems whose papers are submitted for peer review ( Lu et al., 2026 ) . In these systems, ideation is either a brief step before execution or is interleaved with it, as the agent proposes its next change to a working implementation. How the idea is formed matters for what follows: given the same executor, replacing its own ideas with ideas formed separately changes the outcome (§ 5.2 ). Furthermore, the diversity of an agent’s ideas predicts its
research performance on MLE-bench ( Audran-Reiss et al., 2025 ) .
blocks.zh:
AI科学家,LLM代理提出研究想法,执行这些想法并报告结果,已经从演示转向其论文提交同行评审的系统(Lu等,2026年). 在这些系统中,想法要么是执行前的短暂步骤,要么与之互通,因为代理人提议下一步改为工作执行。 如何形成以下概念:赋予同一执行人,用单独形成的想法取而代之,改变结果(第5.2节)。 此外,代理人思想的多样性预示着其
关于MLE-bench的研究业绩(Audran-Reiss等人,2025年)。

blocks.en: Current ideation agents fall short in two opposite ways. Agents prompted to be bold produce ideas that experts judge more novel than human ideas but slightly weaker on feasibility ( Si et al., 2025 ) , and the same agent is the least feasible of those we compare (§ 5.1 ). The ideation stages of end-to-end AI scientists sit at the other end: run on their own, they produce the most feasible ideas we measure and, for The AI Scientist on GPT-5.4, the least original. These contrasting profiles motivate evaluating originality and effectiveness together, the two criteria of the standard definition of creativity ( Runco & Jaeger, 2012 ) .
blocks.zh: 目前的思想代理人在两个相反的方面都不足. 代理商促使人们大胆地提出一些想法,专家们认为这些想法比人类想法更新颖,但对可行性略微弱一些(Si等,2025年),而同样的代理商是我们比较的其中最不可行的(第5.1节)。 端到端AI科学家的思想阶段坐到另一端:他们独自跑步,产生我们衡量的最可行的想法,对于GPT-5.4上的AI科学家来说,是最不独创的. 这些对比性简介激励着共同评价独创性和有效性,即创造力标准定义的两个标准(Runco & Jaeger,2012年)。

blocks.en:
We address the step before implementation: forming a research proposal by transforming the concepts and relations found in prior work. Theories of creativity describe such transformations, among them bisociation ( Koestler, 1964 ) , analogy ( Gentner, 1983 ) , exploration of a conceptual space ( Boden, 2004 ) and elaboration ( Guilford, 1967 ) . In LLM ideation, such processes are often elicited through prompting ( Gu et al., 2024 ; Shen et al., 2026 ) , while some systems
also retain structured intermediate representations.
This motivates distinguishing the instruction to make a
creative move from an explicit check of its form. Ideation agents also bundle retrieval and multi-round refinement into one pipeline ( Si et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025 ; Hu et al., 2024 ) , making their individual contributions difficult to disentangle. This leaves two questions open: which parts of an ideation process improve its ideas, and how a given idea arose from the literature.
blocks.zh:
我们处理执行前的步骤:通过改变先前工作中发现的概念和关系,形成研究建议。 创造力的理论描述了这种转变,其中包括分化(Keestler,1964年),类比(Gentner,1983年),探索概念空间(Boden,2004年)和阐述(Guilford,1967年). 在LLM思想中,这种过程往往通过催化(Gu等人,2024年;Shen等人,2026年)被引出,而一些系统则被引出.
还保留结构化的中间表述。
这促使人们区分作出以下指示:
创造性地从明确检查其形式入手。 理想剂还将取回和多轮精炼装入一管(Si等,2025;Li等,2025;Hu等,2024),使其个人贡献难以分解. 这留下了两个问题:一个思想过程的哪些部分能改进其思想,以及一个特定思想是如何从文献中产生的.

blocks.en: We introduce the Creative AI Researcher (CAR) . CAR extracts a semantic knowledge graph of problems, methods, results, claims and limitations from the literature retrieved for a topic. An ideation agent then develops a proposal over several rounds, using graph-retrieval tools and the four processes above, which CAR exposes as operators that edit the graph. Each operator has a structural definition that is validated before the edit is applied. The accepted and rejected operations, and the literature entities the final proposal declares, form a trace for every idea.
blocks.zh: 我们介绍创意AI研究员。 CAR从为某一专题检索到的文献中提取出关于问题、方法、结果、主张和限制的语义知识图。 然后,一个构思代理公司在几轮内开发出一个提案,使用图检索工具和上面的四个过程,CAR将它暴露为编辑图的操作员. 每个运算符都有在应用编辑前经过验证的结构定义. 被接受和拒绝的行动,以及文学实体宣布的最后提案,为每一个想法都留下了痕迹。

blocks.en:
Our contributions are: • A decomposition of AI research ideation into literature
grounding, iterative development and explicit creative operators. A ten-condition study on two backbones examines
iteration and the operator layer within this grounded setting,
distinguishing their effects on judged idea quality from
the procedural trace they provide. • CAR, which makes the decomposition testable: four creativity processes implemented as validated, recorded operators over a literature-derived knowledge graph, so that every proposal carries a trace from prior work to the final idea. • An evaluation of CAR on originality and effectiveness, the two criteria of the standard definition of creativity, on three benchmarks, with judge agreement assessed against expert ratings.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Grounding ideation in the literature
blocks.zh: 2.1 文献中的思想依据

blocks.en: Research ideation systems ground ideas in prior work ( Wang et al., 2024 ; Yang et al., 2025 ; Si et al., 2025 ; Baek et al., 2025 ) or through a graph, which selects or forecasts concept pairs ( Gu & Krenn, 2024 ; Gu & Krenn, 2025 ) , conditions generation ( Li et al., 2026b ; Lei et al., 2025 ) , supplies reasoning paths ( Buehler, 2024 ; Ghafarollahi & Buehler, 2025 ) , is extended by the model as it reasons ( Buehler, 2025b ; Buehler, 2025a ) , or holds the ideas themselves, as in Evolving Idea Graphs ( Dong et al., 2026 ) . Evolving Idea Graphs also validates candidate graph edits. CAR focuses on four creative operators with explicit acceptance conditions, recording their accepted and rejected calls as ideas develop.
blocks.zh: 研究思想系统在前作中的地想(王等,2024;杨等,2025;西等,2025;白等,2025;)或通过图来选择或预测概念对(顾克林,2025.). ; 2024; Gu & Krenn, 2025),条件生成(Li等, 2026b; Lei等, 2025), 提供推理路径(Buehler, 2024; Ghafarollahi & Buehler, 2025), 由模型按其原因扩展(Buehler, 2025b; Buehler, 2025a), 或自持思想, 如Evolving Idea Graphs (Dong等, 2026). 正在演进中的思想图也验证候选图编辑. CAR专注于四个具有明确接受条件的创意运营商,记录随着思想的发展,他们被接受和拒绝的呼声.

blocks.en: 2.2 Iterative and agentic ideation
blocks.zh: 2.2 迭代和代理思想

blocks.en:
Chain of Ideas ( Li et al., 2025 ) and Nova ( Hu et al., 2024 ) retrieve and refine seed ideas over several rounds, multi-agent teams assign roles and debate ( Baek et al., 2025 ; Ghafarollahi & Buehler, 2025 ; Swanson et al., 2025 ; Gottweis et al., 2025 ; Su et al., 2025 ) , and end-to-end AI scientists couple ideation to experiment search and writing ( Lu et al., 2026 ; Tang et al., 2025 ; Weng et al., 2026 ) , with evidence from MLE-bench that ideation diversity predicts performance ( Audran-Reiss et al., 2025 ) . Many of these systems develop ideas through natural-language revision and critique before or during experimental execution. CAR develops proposals before execution, combining iterative
reasoning with explicit creative operators whose graph edits
are validated and recorded.
blocks.zh:
思想链(Li等,2025年)和Nova等(Hu等,2024年)在多轮中回收并完善了种子思想,多剂团队分配了角色和辩论(Baek等,2025年;Ghafarolahi和Buehler,2025年;Swanson等,2025年;Gottweis等,2025年;Su等,2025年;端到端AI科学家对实验搜索和写作的想法(Lu等,2026年;Tang等,2025年;Weng等,2026年),其证据来自MLE-bench,思想多样性预测性能(Audran-Reiss等,2025年)。 其中许多系统在实验执行之前或期间通过自然语言的修订和批评来发展思想。 中非共和国在执行前拟订建议,结合迭代
与图形编辑的清晰创意运算符进行推理
验证和记录。

blocks.en: 2.3 Creative operators and traceable reasoning
blocks.zh: 2.3 创意经营者和可追踪推理

blocks.en:
CAR’s operators are named after bisociation ( Koestler, 1964 ) , with a bridge entity from conceptual blending ( Fauconnier & Turner, 2003 ) , structure-mapping analogy ( Gentner, 1983 ) , exploratory creativity ( Boden, 2004 ; Wiggins, 2006 ) and elaboration ( Guilford, 1967 ) . Earlier computational work includes analogy mining ( Hope et al., 2017 ) and bisociative networks ( Ahmed & Fuge, 2018 ) , CHIMERA catalogs recombinations in published papers ( Sternlicht & Hope, 2025 ) , and LLM work elicits such moves through prompting ( Radensky et al., 2026 ; Gu et al., 2024 ; Shen et al., 2026 ) or implements combinational, exploratory and transformative
reasoning over generated thoughts ( Suzuki & Banaei-Kashani, 2025 ) .
Some approaches retain intermediate representations: Radensky et al. (2026) record purpose, mechanism and evaluation facets, while Shen et al. (2026) generate and assess explicit analogies.
Such artifacts make the proposed transformations inspectable,
but do not establish that the final idea depends on them.
This distinction also arises in the faithfulness problem of
chain-of-thought ( Turpin et al., 2023 ; Lanham et al., 2023 ) . Lyu et al. (2023) make reasoning faithful by having an LLM
translate a problem into a symbolic representation, which a deterministic solver executes to obtain the answer.
CAR applies a related principle at the tool boundary: each creative operator must satisfy structural acceptance conditions before its graph edit is applied. The resulting trace records the operations performed,
without establishing their causal necessity to the final proposal.

这些文物使拟议的改造可以检查,

blocks.en: 2.4 Evaluating AI-generated research ideas
blocks.zh: 2.4 评价人工智能产生的研究想法

blocks.en:
Benchmarks pair LLM judges with fixed rubrics ( Ruan et al., 2026 ; Qiu et al., 2025 ) or test whether judges predict later research outcomes ( Ye et al., 2026 ) . Retrieval-grounded checks compare an idea against its nearest published work ( Si et al., 2025 ; Shen et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2026 ; Shahid et al., 2025 ) . Whether LLMs are qualified originality reviewers is contested ( Huang et al., 2025 ) .
We assess agreement between our originality and methodological
novelty judges and the expert ratings of Si et al. (2025) and an adjusted
human-agreement reference, with development-set limitations
discussed in Appendix D .

blocks.en: 3 CAR: Grounded creative iteration over a knowledge graph
blocks.zh: 3 CAR: 以知识图为基础的创意迭代

blocks.en: Figure 1: Overview of CAR. Ground: a typed knowledge graph is extracted from the retrieved literature, repaired and frozen. Iterate: the ideation agent develops an idea with four creative operators, each validated against the graph and applied only when it is successful. Trace: the proposal is stored with its declared literature entities and its accepted and rejected operations.
blocks.zh: 图1:中非共和国概况。 地:从取回的文献中取出打入的知识图,被修复并被冻结. 立体:构思代理开发出由4个创意操作员组成的构思,每个操作员对照图表进行验证,只有在成功时才被应用. Trace:提案存放在其申报的文献实体及其被接受和拒绝的操作中.

blocks.en: CAR has three components (Figure 1 ). Given a research aim, it first builds a semantic knowledge graph (KG) of scientific entities and relations from retrieved literature (§ 3.1 ). An LLM ideation agent then develops ideas over this graph with graph-retrieval tools (§ 3.2 ) and four validated creative operators (§ 3.3 ). Each idea is stored with a trace of the operations and declared literature entities.
blocks.zh: 中非共和国有三个组成部分(图1)。 鉴于一项研究目标,它首先建立了一个科学实体和检索文献关系语义知识图(第3.1节)。 然后,LLM思想代理在这个图上用图检索工具(§ 3.2)和四个经过验证的创意操作员(§ 3.3)来开发想法. 每个想法都存有操作和申报的文献实体的痕迹.

blocks.en: 3.1 Knowledge construction
blocks.zh: 3.1 知识建设

blocks.en: Corpus. For each research task, an LLM queries the Semantic Scholar API in an iterative loop, with search prompts adapted from the Research Ideation Agent ( Si et al., 2025 ) : keyword queries, queries for papers similar to a given paper, and queries for a paper’s references (Appendix K.1.1 ). An LLM scores the retrieved papers for relevance and we retain up to 20 20 papers with the highest relevance scores among those whose full text can be obtained.
blocks.zh: 科普斯(英语:Corpus). 对于每项研究任务,一个LLM在迭接回回回路中查询语义学者API,其中的搜索提示从研究理想代理(Si等,2025年)中改编而来:关键词查询,类似给定论文的论文查询和论文参考查询(Appendix K.1.1.). LLM将检索到的文件评分是否具有相关性,我们保留了多达20份论文,在可获取全文的论文中具有最高相关性。

blocks.en:
Extraction. From each paper an LLM extracts typed entities, each with a technical description, and the relations between them: the paper itself, and its problems, tasks, concepts, assumptions, methods, implementation details, hyperparameters, materials, experiments, metrics, results, claims, limitations and formulas (Appendix K.1.2 ). This follows a view from scientometrics that a paper’s elements are the substrate of original recombination ( Dirk, 1999 ; Luo et al., 2022 ; Zhao & Zhang, 2025 ) . Extracting them as distinct typed entities makes recombination expressible as an explicit operation on the graph. The result is a directed multigraph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) with E ⊆ V × R × V E\subseteq V\times R\times V , where R R is the relation vocabulary produced by extraction. We write V lit = V V_{\mathrm{lit}}=V for these literature nodes and V paper ⊂ V lit V_{\mathrm{paper}}\subset V_{\mathrm{lit}} for paper nodes, which record provenance only. Two repair steps add relations for insufficiently connected entities and merge nodes with matching normalized names and entity types. Neither step introduces new entities (Appendix A ). The graph is built once per topic and frozen.
Each idea starts from this graph, with relation labels permuted in the relation-label-shuffle ablation.
blocks.zh:

blocks.en: The ideation agent reads the graph through three tools. ask_knowledge_graph_exploration_agent delegates a natural-language question to a graph exploration agent adapted from ARK ( Polonuer et al., 2026 ) , which searches the graph by keyword and over one-hop neighborhoods and returns relevant entities with its reasoning for each. get_entity_details returns an entity’s full description given its index, and get_edges_by_entity lists its incident literature edges.

blocks.en: Operator design. Bisociate ( Koestler, 1964 ) connects two existing, unlinked entities through a new bridge entity. The one-edge form ( s , r , o ) (s,r,o) is not allowed, since it only asserts a relation between two concepts the literature already contains, whereas the bridge forces a new concept at their intersection ( Fauconnier & Turner, 2003 ) . Analogize follows structure mapping ( Gentner, 1983 ) : it carries a relation from a source pair to a target pair, and only the target is added to the graph. The source may come from the agent’s own knowledge, since restricting it to the corpus would confine transfer to the retrieved literature. The target must change both endpoints: keeping one fixed ( A : B → C : B A\!:\!B\rightarrow C\!:\!B ) does not carry the relation to a new pair, it only adds C C as another entity related to B B . Explore , after Boden’s exploratory creativity ( Boden, 2004 ) , extends the graph by one step from an existing entity, which may itself be proposed. Elaborate , after Guilford’s elaboration ( Guilford, 1967 ) , adds no entity: it replaces a proposed entity’s description with a more specific one and may tie it to a literature entity through one grounding edge. Every operation therefore attaches to the graph at one or more entities, which is what makes an idea traceable.
blocks.zh: 运营商设计. Bisciate (Keestler, 1964)通过一个新的桥梁实体连接两个已存在而无关联的实体. 不允许单尖形式(s, r, o (s, r, o)),因为它只宣称文献中已经包含的两个概念之间的关系,而桥梁则在它们之间的交汇处施加了一个新的概念(Faconnier & Turner, 2003.)。 仿照结构映射(Gentner,1983年) :它带有从源对到目标对的关系,只有目标被添加到图中. 来源可能来自代理人本身的了解,因为将来源限制在委托书内将仅限于被取回的文献。 目标必须改变两个终点: 保持一个固定(A: B → C : B A\!)! B\rightarrow C\!:\!B)不携带与一对新配对的关系,它只增加了C C作为另一个与B B相关的实体. 探索在博登探索创造力(Boden, 2004)之后, 在Guilford的阐述(Guilford,1967年)之后, 因此,每个行动都附属于一个或多个实体的图表,这就使得一个想法可以追踪。

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4个实验

blocks.en: We frame evaluation with the standard definition of creativity. We first assess (a) the originality and feasibility of CAR’s ideas, and then go beyond feasibility, which is necessary but not sufficient for creativity, to assess (b) their effectiveness as test-metric improvement when executed.
blocks.zh: 我们以创造性的标准定义为评价的框架。 我们首先评估(a) 中非共和国想法的原创性和可行性,然后超越可行性,这是必要的,但不足以创造力,以便评估(b) 在执行时,这些想法作为测试改进的效果。

blocks.en: 4.1 Benchmarks and tasks
blocks.zh: 4.1 基准和任务

blocks.en: LiveIdeaBench ( Ruan et al., 2026 ) contains 1,180 scientific keywords from 22 domains and uses LLM judges to assess the ideas generated for a keyword along dimensions inspired by Guilford’s account of divergent thinking ( Guilford, 1967 ) : originality , feasibility , clarity (how understandable and complete an idea is) and fluency (how distinct a method’s ideas for one keyword are from one another). We select 40 keywords, ten each from the computational, physical, life and social sciences. We report its fifth dimension, flexibility, in Appendix E.2 . Our modifications to the protocol are listed in Appendix C.1 .
blocks.zh: LiveIdea Bench(Ruan等,2026年)载有来自22个域的1,180个科学关键词,并使用LM法官来评估Guilford关于不同思维的叙述(Guilford,1967年)所启发的关于关键词的构思:独创性、可行性、清晰度(一个概念如何可以理解和完整)和流利度(一个关键词的方法的想法如何不同)。 我们从计算、物理、生命和社会科学中选择40个关键词,每个关键词10个。 我们在附录E.2中报告了第五个方面,即灵活性。 我们对议定书的修改载于附录C.1。

blocks.en: FML-bench ( Zou et al., 2026 ) comprises 18 machine learning research tasks in 10 domains, each with a baseline repository, a set of editable files and a held-out test metric, and scores an agent on how far it improves the baseline. All agents edit code and run experiments through the same benchmark-provided tools, so differences between agents reflect their research strategy rather than their tooling. We use the Lite split of eight tasks.
blocks.zh: FML-bench(Zou等,2026年)包括10个领域的18个机器学习研究任务,每个任务都有一个基线存储库,一套可编辑的文件和一个被搁置的测试度量衡,并评分一个代理人如何改进基线. 所有代理编辑代码,并通过同样的基准提供的工具进行实验,因此代理之间的差异反映了他们的研究策略而不是工具. 我们用Lite分出八项任务

blocks.en: BioXArena ( Li et al., 2026a ) is a benchmark of 76 end-to-end biomedical machine learning tasks spanning nine areas, most combining several input modalities. Unlike FML-bench, a task supplies data and a metric but no baseline repository, so an agent must design the pipeline and the method. We use the ten tasks of the benchmark’s human-comparison pilot, which supplies a human reference. One task, cell-type-from-expression, has a label leak that makes it trivially solvable (five of seven entries, including CAR and the human reference, score 1.000 1.000 ). We show it but exclude it from means and win rates.
blocks.zh: BioXArena 生物区 (Li等,2026a)是76个端到端生物医学机器学习任务的基准,跨越了9个领域,大多数结合了几种输入模式. 与FML-bench不同,任务提供数据和一个度量但无基线存储器,因此一个代理必须设计管道和方法. 我们使用基准的人类比较试验的十项任务,这提供了人类的参考。 一项任务,即细胞类型自表达,有标签漏出,使其微乎其微地可以溶解(7个条目中有5个,包括CAR和人类参考,得分为1000 1.000. 我们显示它,但把它排除在手段之外,我们赢得了报酬。

blocks.zh: 4.2 评价尺度

blocks.en: LiveIdeaBench. We follow the benchmark’s LLM-as-a-judge protocol, with its prompts, scales and fluency score map. A panel of three critics from vendors other than the generators’ scores each idea 1 1 – 10 10 for originality (O), feasibility (F) and clarity (C), and judges fluency (Flu.) on every pair of a method’s five ideas for each keyword.

blocks.en: 4.3 Experimental settings
blocks.zh: 4.3 实验设置

blocks.en: LiveIdeaBench. We compare CAR with a single-shot Base LLM (the backbone prompted once with the benchmark’s own idea prompt), the Research Ideation Agent (RIA) ( Si et al., 2025 ) , and the ideation stages of The AI Scientist and The AI Scientist-v2 ( Lu et al., 2026 ) . Each baseline generates in its native format and is normalized afterwards (Appendix B ). RIA draws its retrieved papers from CAR’s corpus of up to 20 20 papers for the keyword, The AI Scientist-v2 runs its own Semantic Scholar search, and The AI Scientist’s ideation stage uses no literature. Every method runs on GPT-5.4 and GLM-5.2, and two numbers given without labels are for these backbones in this order. To lower cost, CAR’s graph exploration agent uses DeepSeek-V4-Pro, and the ideation agent may send it only one natural-language query per idea. We generate up to five ideas per keyword.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
CAR combines literature grounding, iterative development and
explicit creative operators for research ideation. It exceeds
single-shot prompting and The AI Scientist in methodological
novelty and achieves the highest win rate among the evaluated
AI methods on both execution benchmarks. MN point estimates favor CAR over one-step proposal on both backbones, although no MN ablation contrast survives correction for multiple comparisons.
The operators make idea development inspectable, but their
quality benefit beyond free-form iteration is not established.

明确研究想法的创造性操作员。 超过
单发和AI科学家在方法方面

操作者使想法开发可以检查,但
自由形式迭代之外的质量效益没有确定。

blocks.en: AI use statement
blocks.zh: AI 语句

blocks.en:
In this work, we used generative AI tools to design or provide feedback on research methodology or experiments, implement methods, clean and reformat datasets, support qualitative and thematic data analysis, and interpret results. We have not used generative AI tools to generate synthetic data sets, help develop theoretical models or conceptual frameworks or propose or refine hypotheses, and the remaining required disclosure tasks, namely to formulate mathematical claims, provide critical ingredients for proving mathematical claims, assist in the writing of proofs, and assist with translation, are not applicable to this work. The statement above describes how we used AI to carry out
this study and write the paper. Separately, generating research
proposals is the experimental task performed by CAR and
the comparison methods. Additionally, we used generative AI tools to formulate questions for surveys or interviews, create or modify scientific figures or images, suggest experimental parameters, create or edit software code, create artifacts, draft parts of a research paper, summarize or analyze existing literature, discover research topics or identify gaps, brainstorm, source or search for information, edit a research paper to improve readability, identify relevant literature, format references, suggest a structure for a research paper, and propose a title or keywords for a research paper.
We have reviewed all AI-assisted work. We take responsibility for checking AI-assisted text, code and analyses against the underlying sources and experimental records. AI-assisted code was reviewed and tested by the authors. AI-drafted text and literature summaries were checked against the cited papers by the authors, and the research-proposal-type labels in Appendix F.2 are human labels. We take responsibility for the final content of this work, including text, claims and artifacts produced with the aid of generative AI.

在这项工作中,我们使用基因AI工具来设计或提供研究方法或实验的反馈,实施方法,清理和重塑数据集,支持定性和专题数据分析,并解释结果. 我们没有使用基因AI工具来生成合成数据集,帮助开发理论模型或概念框架,或提出或完善假说,其余需要的披露任务,即提出数学索赔,提供数学索赔的关键要素,协助编写证据,并协助翻译,都不适用于这项工作. 以上陈述说明了我们如何利用大赦国际开展

blocks.en: Ethics statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en:
This work automates part of research ideation. Generated ideas are untested proposals and may be wrong, infeasible or unsafe if pursued. CAR records which literature entities each idea builds on, which supports attribution to prior work, but it does not replace a literature review by the researcher. A small number of generated biomedical ideas were refused by one judge’s provider content filter and are excluded and counted (Appendix E.1 ).
The literature corpora are built from papers obtained as arXiv sources, as open-access PDFs, or under the authors’ institutional subscriptions. Full texts are used only for entity and relation extraction and are not redistributed. We release paper identifiers, the extracted knowledge graphs, prompts and derived data, not the papers themselves.
The human ratings we use for instrument validation are the publicly released data of Si et al. (2025) . The idea-type labels (Appendix F.2 ) were provided by three members of the authors’ group who labeled anonymized abstracts.
blocks.zh:
这部作品将研究思想的一部分自动化. 产生的想法是未经检验的建议,如果推行,可能是错误的、不可行的或不安全的。 CAR记录了每个想法所依赖的文献实体,支持将作品归属于之前的作品,但并不取代研究者对文献的审查. 少数产生的生物医学思想被一名法官的提供者内容过滤器所拒绝,被排除在外和计算(附录E.1)。
文献公司是根据作为arXiv来源、公开访问PDF或作者机构订阅而获得的论文编写的。 全文仅用于实体和关系提取,不重新分配。 我们释放出纸质识别器,提取出的知识图,提示和衍生出的数据,而不是文件本身.
我们用于仪器验证的人类评级是Si等人(2025年)公开发布的数据. 创意类型的标签(附录F.2)由作者小组的三名成员提供,他们给匿名摘要贴上标签。

blocks.en: Reproducibility statement
blocks.zh: 可复制说明

blocks.en: The main prompts are given in Appendix K , baseline fidelity and output normalization in Appendix B , and models, providers, cut-off dates, decoding settings and keyword lists in Appendix C . We will release code, the per-keyword paper identifiers and knowledge graphs, all generated ideas with their operator traces, all judge outputs, and the scripts that regenerate every table from these files. Hosted LLMs are not deterministic, so we pin providers for open-weight models and report the variation across three independent end-to-end draws of the methodological novelty instrument (Appendix D ). The number of ideas behind each MN result, and the ideas excluded for missing retrieval evidence or judge refusals, are given in Appendix E.1 .

blocks.en: Appendix A Knowledge graph repair and entity resolution
blocks.zh: 知识图修复和实体分辨率

blocks.en:
Per-paper extraction can leave scientific entities without relations
to other non-paper entities and can represent the same entity under
different names. We apply relation repair within each paper and
entity resolution across the assembled graph.
blocks.zh:
纸质提取可以让科学实体失去关系
其他非文件实体可代表同一实体
不同名称。 我们在每张纸里都应用了修复关系
整个组图的实体分辨率。

blocks.en:
Relation repair (within a paper). We measure relation coverage as the fraction of non-paper
nodes incident to at least one edge whose endpoints are both
non-paper nodes. Edges incident to paper nodes record provenance
and are excluded from this measure. When coverage falls below 80 % 80\% , an LLM proposes additional relations using the extracted

the threshold.

blocks.en:
On BioXArena’s pan-cancer survival task, a bisociate operation connects Guided Mixture of Experts with a discrete-time
survival loss through interval-specialized expert routing .
The code snapshot with the highest validation score
implements a mixture of experts with a gate conditioned
on cancer type and survival interval.
Specifically, the gate takes concatenated cancer and
interval embeddings and gene-availability indicators,
then assigns softmax weights to the expert outputs.

post-hoc scoring function, while the standard cross-entropy

blocks.en: Appendix J Limitations
blocks.zh: 附录J 限制

blocks.en:
Literature and extraction. CAR builds its graph from papers whose full text it can obtain.
In our experiments, some papers that could not be downloaded
automatically were retrieved manually through institutional
subscriptions. Deployments without equivalent access may
construct different or less extensive corpora.
Entities and relations are extracted by an LLM, and we do not
measure extraction accuracy against expert annotation.
Relation repair addresses missing connectivity but does not
verify scientific correctness. Name-based merging can leave
semantically overlapping entities separate.
blocks.zh:
文学与取出. CAR用它可以获得的全文的纸张来绘制其图表。
在我们的实验中,有些论文无法下载
通过机构自动检索
订阅. 没有同等准入的部署可能
构建不同的或不太广泛的公司。
实体和关系由LLM提取,我们没有
对照专家注释测量提取精度。
连接修复地址缺失, 但没有
核实科学正确性。 基于名称的合并可以离开
严重重叠的实体分开。

blocks.en:
Cost. Graph construction and iterative ideation introduce additional
calls and token usage. Recorded generation costs vary by
backbone and method (Appendix I ).
Building the graph once per topic amortizes construction
across ideas, but not the per-idea reasoning and retrieval
costs. The reported estimates exclude evaluation and
unrecorded failed attempts, so they are not complete
end-to-end costs.

from explicit operators beyond free-form iteration.

one backbone, so these results should not be interpreted
as showing that the components have no effect.
The trace records tool interactions, accepted and rejected
operations, and declared literature entities.
Its guarantees are procedural and structural.
An entity appearing in a tool result does not establish
that the agent used it meaningfully, and an accepted
operation need not be scientifically sound.
The trace does not establish that each entity or operation
was causally necessary to the proposal.

blocks.en:
Evaluation. Idea quality is assessed by LLM judges, without direct human
evaluation of the generated ideas’ quality.
Agreement with expert ratings is assessed on a separate
sample of NLP proposals. This sample also informed development
of the methodological novelty evaluator, so its reported
agreement is not independent held-out validation.
The adjusted split-half human-agreement estimate is a
reference, not a second observed expert panel, and the
comparison does not establish equivalence to human reviewers.
Retrieval-based novelty is conditional on the evidence found
and cannot establish novelty across the wider literature.

The 40 40 -keyword sample limits precision, especially for

Results differ between backbones, and nonsignificant

blocks.en: Knowledge Extraction Prompt I want to extract structured, detailed scientific knowledge from the full text of a scientific paper. Your output will populate a knowledge graph with scientific units, concepts, and relations. Extract the technically important scientific units, concepts, and relations with high coverage, while avoiding generic background mentions that do not help connect the graph. WORKFLOW: 1. Scientific Units Extraction: - Paper: A dense, technical summary of the paper’s core contributions (2-3 paragraphs). This paper node will act as the anchor for knowledge extracted from this paper. The graph builder will connect it to the paper’s extracted problems, methods, experiments, results, claims, limitations, and formulas, while entity-entity relations may also connect those nodes directly. - Problems: Specific challenges, limitations of prior work, or research gaps addressed. - Methods: Exact names of novel algorithms, architectures, protocols, or methodologies proposed or substantially modified by this paper. Do not put baselines, prior work, off-the-shelf architectures, standard preprocessing steps, optimizers, or calibration procedures here; put them in the "concepts" list with type "method". - Put a technique in top-level "methods" only if the paper proposes it, substantially modifies it, or treats it as a named component of its contribution. Put prior architectures, baselines, standard preprocessing steps, optimizers, metrics, datasets, and off-the-shelf calibration procedures in "concepts" with the most specific type. - Experiments: Specific evaluation protocols, benchmark settings, ablation studies, simulation studies, lab assays, user studies, or analysis procedures conducted by the paper. An experiment is the setup/procedure, not the measured outcome. - Results: Concrete empirical findings or observations, preferably with metrics, datasets, conditions, confidence intervals, comparisons, or qualitative observations. A result is evidence, not the broad claim it supports. - Claims: Declarative scientific assertions made by the paper, usually supported by results. A claim states what the authors argue is true; it is not a raw metric result. - Limitations: Explicitly stated weaknesses, failure modes, assumptions, boundary conditions, threats to validity, negative findings, or future-work gaps. 2. Mathematical Formulas Extraction: - Extract crucial formulas (in LaTeX) that define the methods or problems. - Provide a summary and TeX for each formula. 3. Scientific Concepts Extraction: - Method: A prior algorithm, baseline model, experimental protocol, or technique (e.g., "diffusion model", "crispr-cas9", "x-ray crystallography"). - Metric: A quantitative measure of performance or property (e.g., "fid score", "binding affinity", "tensile strength"). - Task: The specific application or problem being addressed (e.g., "image generation", "protein folding", "alloy synthesis"). - Material: A dataset, software library, biological sample, or physical resource (e.g., "cifar-10", "escherichia coli", "graphene"). - Assumption: Theoretical preconditions, data assumptions, or simplifications (e.g., "i.i.d. data", "ideal gas", "incompressible fluid"). - Hyperparameter: Key implementation parameters or constants (e.g., "learning rate", "annealing temperature", "catalyst concentration"). - Implementation Detail: Specific engineering choices or procedural tweaks (e.g., "layer normalization", "centrifugation speed", "quenching rate"). - Concept: General scientific terms, mechanisms, artifacts, failure modes, or theoretical constructs that don’t fit the above (e.g., "entropy", "homeostasis", "manifold") 4. Scientific Relations Extraction: - IMPORTANT: Link the Problems, Methods, Experiments, Results, Claims, Limitations, Concepts, and Formulas to one another using relations. - Relation coverage requirement: every important non-paper scientific unit or concept should participate in at least one non-paper relation. Prefer unit-concept, unit-unit, and concept-concept edges over paper-to-concept scaffolding. - If a formula is important enough to extract, include at least one explicit relation connecting the formula to the method, metric, problem, concept, experiment, result, claim, or limitation it defines, formalizes, models, computes, optimizes, constrains, or evaluates. - Prioritize relations that connect methods to problems, experiments to methods/datasets/metrics, results to experiments/claims, claims to evidence, limitations to affected methods/settings, and concepts to the mechanisms or assumptions they influence. - Define the relation name precisely and concisely, and provide a detailed relation description. Explain how and why they are related in detail. - Account for 6 types of relations when they are supported by the paper: taxonomic (e.g., "is variant of", "is subtype of", "generalizes"), compositional (e.g., "contains component", "combines with"), mechanistic (e.g., "causes", "regularizes", "constrains", "formalizes", "calibrates", "inhibits", "stabilizes", "modulates"), methodological (e.g., "trains on", "optimizes", "evaluates on", "defines metric", "applies to"), evidential (e.g., "supports claim", "contradicts claim", "qualifies claim"), and evaluative (e.g., "outperforms", "improves metric", "fails under", "compares against"). Use the domain-appropriate label that most precisely describes the scientific relationship. These examples are illustrative, not exhaustive — use domain-native terms (e.g., "degrades", "binds to", "encodes") when they are more accurate. - Avoid overly generic labels such as "uses", "solves", "produces", "based on", or "related to" when a more specific label exists. - For example, link a Method to the Problem it addresses, or a Result to the Method that achieved it via "outperforms" or "improves metric". GENERAL GUIDELINES: - Return only a valid JSON object. Do not include markdown fences, comments, prose, trailing commas, or ellipses. - Use exactly these top-level keys: "paper", "problems", "methods", "experiments", "results", "claims", "limitations", "formulas", "concepts", "relations". - All top-level list fields must be arrays. If nothing is found for a field, return []. - Be thorough but selective. Aim for high coverage of technically important information, not exhaustive extraction of every mentioned term. - Extract enough concepts and relations to represent the paper’s scientific structure. - Extract enough non-paper relations for the graph to be dominated by scientific structure rather than document provenance. - Avoid isolated concepts. Only extract a standalone concept if it has a specific technical summary and either participates in at least one non-paper relation or is necessary context for understanding a formula, method, experiment, result, claim, or limitation. - Do not extract generic background concepts merely because they are mentioned. - Ensure all extracted scientific knowledge is accurately represented. - Provide accurate and technical details in the entity summaries and relation descriptions. - Ensure mathematical precision for formulas (use LaTeX if needed). - Entity and relation names must be concise, atomic phrases (1-5 words) and in lowercase to prevent duplicates. Do NOT use full sentences as entity names. Put detailed explanations in the ’summary’ field. - Do not duplicate the same scientific object across multiple top-level lists. Use the most specific unit type: proposed contributions go in methods, prior/background methods go in concepts, empirical procedures go in experiments, measurements go in results, and interpretations go in claims. - Ensure all keys are present even if lists are empty. - Extract specific values for hyperparameters and specific implementation choices as context for relations. - Before returning, internally check that proposed methods are linked to the problems, claims, experiments, or limitations they address; experiments are linked to the methods, datasets/materials, metrics, and results they evaluate; results are linked to the experiments that produced them and the claims they support or qualify; claims are linked to supporting results or reasoning; limitations are linked to affected methods, experiments, datasets/materials, assumptions, or claims; important concepts are linked through supported taxonomic, compositional, mechanistic, methodological, evidential, or evaluative relations; and generic concepts that remain isolated are removed. I have retrieved the following content from the paper ’{paper title}’: {content} Please return a valid JSON object with the following structure. Each array may contain zero, one, or many objects of the shown form. The single object shown in each array is only a template; include as many objects as are supported by the paper. { "paper": { "name": "{paper title}", "summary": "detailed summary text" }, "problems": [ { "name": "specific problem statement", "summary": "detailed problem description (MUST include specific context, datasets, values, or conditional parameters)", "relation_description": "edge-specific explanation of how the paper frames, motivates, or operationalizes this problem, including the task setting, failure of prior work, or research gap when available" } ], "methods": [ { "name": "method name", "summary": "detailed method description (MUST include specific context, datasets, values, or conditional parameters)", "relation_description": "edge-specific explanation of what the paper newly proposes or modifies in this method, and which problem, claim, experiment, or limitation it is meant to address" } ], "experiments": [ { "name": "specific experiment, evaluation, ablation, assay, simulation, or analysis name", "summary": "detailed experiment setup/procedure description (MUST include specific datasets, baselines, metrics, controls, conditions, sample sizes, or implementation settings when available)", "relation_description": "edge-specific explanation of the setup/procedure run by the paper and what method, dataset, metric, claim, or hypothesis it evaluates" } ], "results": [ { "name": "quantitative or qualitative result", "summary": "detailed result description (MUST include specific context, datasets, values, or conditional parameters)", "relation_description": "edge-specific explanation of the measurement or observation reported, the condition under which it was obtained, and what claim, method, or comparison it supports or contradicts" } ], "claims": [ { "name": "declarative scientific claim", "summary": "detailed claim description, including what the paper asserts and the conditions or scope under which the claim is meant to hold", "relation_description": "edge-specific explanation of the evidence, reasoning, experiment, or result in the paper that supports this assertion" } ], "limitations": [ { "name": "specific limitation, failure mode, assumption, or open gap", "summary": "detailed limitation description, including affected methods, datasets, settings, assumptions, or boundary conditions when available", "relation_description": "edge-specific explanation of the assumption, failure case, missing evidence, scope boundary, or unresolved gap that makes this a limitation" } ], "formulas": [ { "name": "formula name or label", "summary": "what does this formula represent", "tex": "latex string" } ], "concepts": [ { "name": "concept name", "type": "method|metric|task|material|assumption| hyperparameter|implementation_detail|concept", "summary": "detailed definition, value, or description of the concept (MUST include specific context, datasets, values, or conditional parameters)" } ], "relations": [ { "subject": "entity name", "object": "entity name", "relation": "concise, domain-specific relation label (not generic like ’uses’ or ’related to’)", "description": "edge-specific technical explanation of exactly how and why the subject relates to the object in this paper (MUST include specific context, datasets, values, or conditional parameters)" } ] }
blocks.zh: 知识提取提示 我想从一份科学论文的全文中提取有条理,详细的科学知识. 您的输出将包含一个包含科学单位,概念和关系的知识图. 摘录具有重要技术意义的科学单位、概念和高覆盖率的关系,同时避免一般背景提及无助于连接图表。 工作流程:1. 科学单位 提取: -- 文件:文件核心贡献的密集技术总结(2至3段)。 本文节点将作为本文所取出的知识的锚. 图表构建器将把它与论文提取出的问题、方法、实验、结果、主张、限制和公式相连接,而实体-实体关系也可能直接连接这些节点。 - 问题:具体挑战、以前工作的局限性或研究差距。 - 方法:本文件所提出或作重大修改的新算法、结构、协议或方法的确切名称。 不要在此放入基线,前作,现成的架构,标准预处理步骤,优化器,或校正程序;将其与"方法"同入"概念"列表. - 只有在论文提出、实质性修改或将其当作其贡献的一个有名的组成部分时,才能在顶层“方法”中采用技术。 将以前的架构,基线,标准预处理步骤,优化器,度量衡,数据集,以及现成的校正程序放入"概念"中,最具体的类型. - 实验:具体评价协议、基准设置、衰减研究、模拟研究、实验室分析、用户研究或论文进行的分析程序。 实验是设置/程序,而不是测量的结果. - 成果:具体的经验结论或观测结果,最好有衡量标准、数据集、条件、信任间隔、比较或质量观测。 结果就是证据,而不是它所支持的广泛主张。 - 索赔:论文所作的科学声明,通常有结果支持。 一项申诉说,提交人的论点是真实的;这不是一个初步的结果。 - 限制:明确指出弱点、失败模式、假设、边界条件、对有效性的威胁、负面结论或未来工作的差距。 2. 数学公式提取: - 提取关键公式(在LaTeX中)来定义方法或问题. - 为每个公式提供摘要和TeX。 3. 科学概念提取法:- 方法:一种先行算法,基准模型,实验协议,或技术(如"扩散模型","crispr-cas9","x-射线晶体学"等). - 量子:对性能或属性(如"纤维分","绑定亲和","强度"等)进行定量测量. - 任务:正在处理的具体应用或问题(如"图像生成","蛋白质折叠","合金合成"等). - 材料:一个数据集,软件库,生物样本,或物理资源(如"cifar-10","escherichia coli","graphene"). - 假设:理论先决条件,数据假设,或简化(如"一一数据","理想气体","不可压缩液体"等). - 超参数: 关键执行参数或常数(如"学习率","放出温度","催化浓度"等). - 实施详情:具体工程选择或程序修饰(如"层平通","离心速度","平通率"等). - 概念:一般科学术语、机制、文物、失败模式,或不符合上述条件的理论构造(例如“entropy”、“homostasis”、“manyfold”) 4. 科学关系提取: - 重要性:利用关系将问题、方法、实验、结果、要求、限制、概念和公式联系起来。 - 关系覆盖要求:每个重要的非论文科学单位或概念应至少参与一个非论文关系。 偏好单位-概念,单位-单位,概念-概念的边缘比从纸到概念的脚手架. - 如果一个公式足够重要,可以提取,至少包括一个明确的关系,将公式与方法、度量、问题、概念、实验、结果、主张或限制联系起来,它定义、正规化、模型、计算、优化、约束或评价。 - 优先处理将方法与问题联系起来的关系,将实验与方法/数据集/计量方法联系起来,将结果与实验/主张联系起来,对证据的主张,对受影响方法/设定的限制,以及对其影响的机制或假设的概念。 - 准确和简明地界定关系名称,并提供详细的关系说明。 详细解释如何和为什么它们相互关联。 - 6种关系在得到论文支持时的核算:分类学(如"是"的变体","是"的子类型","通论"),组成学(如"包含成分","与",机械学(如"原因","正规","约束","正规","校正","隐性","稳定","调制","方法"等),方法学(如"trains on","优化","评价"定律","应用到"),证据学(如"支持要求","矛盾要求"),评价学(如"偏差","改进度",衡量"下失败","相比"等). 使用最准确地描述科学关系的适合域名的标签. 这些实例是说明性的,并非详尽无遗的——当它们更准确时,使用域内术语(如"降级","宾入","编码"等). - 当存在更具体的标签时,避免过于笼统的标签,如“使用”、“解决办法”、“生产”、“基于”或“相关”。 - 例如,将方法与它处理的问题联系起来,或将结果与通过“执行”或“改进度量”实现的方法联系起来。 - 仅返回一个有效的JSON对象。 不包括下标栅栏、评论、道具、后标或椭圆等。 准确使用这些顶级密钥:"纸","问题","方法","实验","结果","要求","限制","公式","概念","关系". - 所有顶级列表字段必须是数组。 如果一个字段没有找到,请返回。 目标是高覆盖率地提供技术方面的重要信息,而不是详尽无遗地取出每一个提到的术语。 - 提取足以代表论文科学结构的概念和关系。 - 提取足够的非文件关系,使图表以科学结构而不是文件来源为主。 - 避免孤立的概念。 只有在有具体的技术摘要并参与至少一种非文件关系或为理解一种公式、方法、试验、结果、主张或限制所必需的背景时,才提取一个独立的概念。 不要仅仅因为提到而取出一般背景概念。 - 确保准确反映所有获得的科学知识。 - 在实体摘要和关系说明中提供准确和技术细节。 - 确保公式的数学精确性(必要时使用LaTeX)。 - 实体和关系名称必须简洁,原子短语(1至5个字)并用小写来防止重复。 不使用完整句子作为实体名称 。 在 " 总结 " 领域作出详细解释。 在多个顶级列表中不要重复相同的科学对象. 使用最具体的单位类型:提议的贡献按方法进行,前/后方法按概念进行,经验程序按实验进行,计量按结果进行,解释按索赔进行。 - 确保所有密钥都存在,即使列表为空。 - 提取超参数的具体值和具体的执行选择,作为关系的背景。 - 在返回之前,进行内部核查,以确定拟议方法与它们所处理的问题、要求、实验或限制相关联;实验与它们评价的方法、数据集/材料、衡量尺度和结果相关联;结果与产生这些方法的实验及其支持或符合条件的要求相关联;索赔与支持结果或推理相关联;限制与受影响的方法、实验、数据集/材料、假设或主张相关联;通过支持分类、组成、机械、方法、证据或评价关系等重要概念相关联;删除仍然孤立的通用概念。 我从论文标题中找到以下内容: [内容] 请返回以下结构的有效 JSON 对象 。 每个阵列可能包含0,1,或显示形式的许多对象. 每个阵列中显示的单个对象只是模板;包含尽可能多的被纸张支持的对象. o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- “o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- “o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- “o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o- o-

blocks.zh: 我想从一份科学论文的全文中提取有条理,详细的科学知识.

blocks.en: Your output will populate a knowledge graph with scientific units, concepts, and relations. Extract the technically important scientific units, concepts, and relations with high coverage, while avoiding generic background mentions that do not help connect the graph.
blocks.zh: 您的输出将包含一个包含科学单位,概念和关系的知识图. 摘录具有重要技术意义的科学单位、概念和高覆盖率的关系,同时避免一般背景提及无助于连接图表。

blocks.en: WORKFLOW:
blocks.zh: 工作时间:

blocks.en: 1. Scientific Units Extraction:
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 科学单位 :

blocks.en: - Paper: A dense, technical summary of the paper’s core contributions (2-3 paragraphs). This paper node will act as the anchor for knowledge extracted from this paper. The graph builder will connect it to the paper’s extracted problems, methods, experiments, results, claims, limitations, and formulas, while entity-entity relations may also connect those nodes directly.
blocks.zh: - 纸张: 文件核心贡献的密集技术摘要(2至3段)。 本文节点将作为本文所取出的知识的锚. 图表构建器将把它与论文提取出的问题、方法、实验、结果、主张、限制和公式相连接,而实体-实体关系也可能直接连接这些节点。

blocks.en: - Problems: Specific challenges, limitations of prior work, or research gaps addressed.
blocks.zh: - 问题:具体挑战、以前工作的局限性或研究差距。

blocks.en: - Methods: Exact names of novel algorithms, architectures, protocols, or methodologies proposed or substantially modified by this paper. Do not put baselines, prior work, off-the-shelf architectures, standard preprocessing steps, optimizers, or calibration procedures here; put them in the "concepts" list with type "method".
blocks.zh: - 方法: 本文所提出或作实质性修改的小说算法,架构,协议或方法的确切名称. 不要在此放入基线,前作,现成的架构,标准预处理步骤,优化器,或校正程序;将其与"方法"同入"概念"列表.

blocks.en: - Put a technique in top-level "methods" only if the paper proposes it, substantially modifies it, or treats it as a named component of its contribution. Put prior architectures, baselines, standard preprocessing steps, optimizers, metrics, datasets, and off-the-shelf calibration procedures in "concepts" with the most specific type.
blocks.zh: - 说吧 在顶层"方法"中放入一种技术,只有在论文提出,实质性地修改,或者把它当作其贡献的一个被命名的组成部分时. 将以前的架构,基线,标准预处理步骤,优化器,度量衡,数据集,以及现成的校正程序放入"概念"中,最具体的类型.

blocks.en: - Experiments: Specific evaluation protocols, benchmark settings, ablation studies, simulation studies, lab assays, user studies, or analysis procedures conducted by the paper. An experiment is the setup/procedure, not the measured outcome.
blocks.zh: - 实验: 具体的评价协议,基准设置,消化研究,模拟研究,实验室化验,用户研究,或由论文进行的分析程序. 实验是设置/程序,而不是测量的结果.

blocks.en: - Results: Concrete empirical findings or observations, preferably with metrics, datasets, conditions, confidence intervals, comparisons, or qualitative observations. A result is evidence, not the broad claim it supports.
blocks.zh: - 结果: 具体的经验性结论或观测结果,最好有衡量标准、数据集、条件、置信间隔、比较或定性观测。 结果就是证据,而不是它所支持的广泛主张。

blocks.en: - Claims: Declarative scientific assertions made by the paper, usually supported by results. A claim states what the authors argue is true; it is not a raw metric result.
blocks.zh: - 索赔:论文所作的科学声明,通常有结果支持。 一项申诉说,提交人的论点是真实的;这不是一个初步的结果。

blocks.en: - Limitations: Explicitly stated weaknesses, failure modes, assumptions, boundary conditions, threats to validity, negative findings, or future-work gaps.
blocks.zh: - 限制:明确指出弱点、失败模式、假设、边界条件、对有效性的威胁、负面结论或未来工作的差距。

blocks.en: 2. Mathematical Formulas Extraction:
blocks.zh: 2. 数学公式提取:

blocks.en: - Extract crucial formulas (in LaTeX) that define the methods or problems.
blocks.zh: - 提取定义方法或问题的关键公式(在LaTeX中)。

blocks.en: - Provide a summary and TeX for each formula.
blocks.zh: - 为每个公式提供摘要和TeX。

blocks.en: 3. Scientific Concepts Extraction:
blocks.zh: 3个 科学概念提取:

blocks.en: - Method: A prior algorithm, baseline model, experimental protocol, or technique (e.g., "diffusion model", "crispr-cas9", "x-ray crystallography").
blocks.zh: - 方法: 前作算法,基准模型,实验协议,或技术(如"分化模型","crispr-cas9","x射线晶体学"等).

blocks.en: - Metric: A quantitative measure of performance or property (e.g., "fid score", "binding affinity", "tensile strength").
blocks.zh: - 量级: 性能或属性的量化度量(如"fid分","绑定的亲和","高度强度"等).

blocks.en: - Task: The specific application or problem being addressed (e.g., "image generation", "protein folding", "alloy synthesis").
blocks.zh: - 任务:正在处理的具体应用或问题(如"图像生成","蛋白质折叠","合金合成"等).

blocks.en: - Material: A dataset, software library, biological sample, or physical resource (e.g., "cifar-10", "escherichia coli", "graphene").
blocks.zh: - 材料: 一个数据集,软件库,生物样本,或者物理资源(如"cifar-10","escherichia coli","graphene").

blocks.en: - Assumption: Theoretical preconditions, data assumptions, or simplifications (e.g., "i.i.d. data", "ideal gas", "incompressible fluid").
blocks.zh: - 假设:理论先决条件,数据假设,或简化(如"一一数据","理想气体","不可压缩液体"等).

blocks.en: - Hyperparameter: Key implementation parameters or constants (e.g., "learning rate", "annealing temperature", "catalyst concentration").
blocks.zh: - 超参数: 关键执行参数或常数(如"学习率","放出温度","催化浓度"等).

blocks.en: - Implementation Detail: Specific engineering choices or procedural tweaks (e.g., "layer normalization", "centrifugation speed", "quenching rate").
blocks.zh: - 实施详情:特定的工程选择或程序修饰(如"层态","离心速度","平速"等).

blocks.en: - Concept: General scientific terms, mechanisms, artifacts, failure modes, or theoretical constructs that don’t fit the above (e.g., "entropy", "homeostasis", "manifold")
blocks.zh: - 概念:一般科学术语、机制、文物、失败模式,或不符合上述条件的理论构造(如: "entropy"、 "homostasis"、 "manyfold")

blocks.en: 4. Scientific Relations Extraction:
blocks.zh: 4. 科学关系提取:

blocks.en: - IMPORTANT: Link the Problems, Methods, Experiments, Results, Claims, Limitations, Concepts, and Formulas to one another using relations.
blocks.zh: - 重要性:利用关系将问题、方法、实验、结果、要求、限制、概念和公式联系起来。

blocks.en: - Relation coverage requirement: every important non-paper scientific unit or concept should participate in at least one non-paper relation. Prefer unit-concept, unit-unit, and concept-concept edges over paper-to-concept scaffolding.
blocks.zh: - 关系覆盖要求:每个重要的非论文科学单位或概念应至少参与一个非论文关系。 偏好单位-概念,单位-单位,概念-概念的边缘比从纸到概念的脚手架.

blocks.en: - If a formula is important enough to extract, include at least one explicit relation connecting the formula to the method, metric, problem, concept, experiment, result, claim, or limitation it defines, formalizes, models, computes, optimizes, constrains, or evaluates.
blocks.zh: - 说吧 如果一个公式足够重要可以提取,则至少包括一个将公式与方法,度量,问题,概念,实验,结果,要求,或限制联系起来的明确关系,它定义,正规化,模型,计算,优化,约束,或评价.

blocks.en: - Prioritize relations that connect methods to problems, experiments to methods/datasets/metrics, results to experiments/claims, claims to evidence, limitations to affected methods/settings, and concepts to the mechanisms or assumptions they influence.
blocks.zh: - 优先处理将方法与问题联系起来的关系,将实验与方法/数据集/计量方法联系起来,将结果与实验/主张联系起来,对证据的主张,对受影响方法/设定的限制,以及将概念与其影响的机制或假设联系起来。

blocks.en: - Define the relation name precisely and concisely, and provide a detailed relation description. Explain how and why they are related in detail.
blocks.zh: - 准确和简明地界定关系名称,并提供详细的关系说明。 详细解释如何和为什么它们相互关联。

blocks.en: - Account for 6 types of relations when they are supported by the paper:
blocks.zh: - 在文件支持的情况下,考虑6种关系:

blocks.en: taxonomic (e.g., "is variant of", "is subtype of", "generalizes"),
blocks.zh: 分类学(如"是"的变体,"是"的子类型,"通论"),

blocks.en: compositional (e.g., "contains component", "combines with"),
blocks.zh: 组成(例如“包含组件”、“与”),

blocks.en: mechanistic (e.g., "causes", "regularizes", "constrains", "formalizes", "calibrates", "inhibits", "stabilizes", "modulates"),
blocks.zh: 机械化(如"原因","正统","约束","形式","校正","不规则","稳定","调制"等),

blocks.en: methodological (e.g., "trains on", "optimizes", "evaluates on", "defines metric", "applies to"),
blocks.zh: 方法(例如: "trains on","优化","评价","定义度量","应用到"),

blocks.en: evidential (e.g., "supports claim", "contradicts claim", "qualifies claim"),
blocks.zh: 证据(例如, " 支持索赔 " 、 " 争议索赔 " 、 " 等同索赔 " ),

blocks.en: and evaluative (e.g., "outperforms", "improves metric", "fails under", "compares against").
blocks.zh: 和评价(例如“执行”、“改进度量”、“失败”、“比较”)。

blocks.en: Use the domain-appropriate label that most precisely describes the scientific relationship. These examples are illustrative, not exhaustive — use domain-native terms (e.g., "degrades", "binds to", "encodes") when they are more accurate.
blocks.zh: 使用最准确地描述科学关系的适合域名的标签. 这些实例是说明性的,并非详尽无遗的——当它们更准确时,使用域内术语(如"降级","宾入","编码"等).

blocks.en: - Avoid overly generic labels such as "uses", "solves", "produces", "based on", or "related to" when a more specific label exists.
blocks.zh: - 当存在更具体的标签时,避免过于笼统的标签,如“使用”、“解决办法”、“生产”、“基于”或“相关”。

blocks.en: - For example, link a Method to the Problem it addresses, or a Result to the Method that achieved it via "outperforms" or "improves metric".
blocks.zh: - 例如,将方法与它处理的问题联系起来,或将结果与通过“执行”或“改进度量”实现的方法联系起来。

blocks.en: GENERAL GUIDELINES:
blocks.zh: 一般准则:

blocks.en: - Return only a valid JSON object. Do not include markdown fences, comments, prose, trailing commas, or ellipses.
blocks.zh: - 返回一个有效的JSON对象。 不包括打下标记的栅栏,评论,道具,后接逗号,或椭圆.

blocks.en: - Use exactly these top-level keys: "paper", "problems", "methods", "experiments", "results", "claims", "limitations", "formulas", "concepts", "relations".
blocks.zh: - 准确使用这些顶级密钥:"纸","问题","方法","实验","结果","要求","限制","公式","概念","关系".

blocks.en: - All top-level list fields must be arrays. If nothing is found for a field, return [].
blocks.zh: - 所有顶级列表字段必须是数组。 如果一个字段没有找到,请返回 [].

blocks.en: - Be thorough but selective. Aim for high coverage of technically important information, not exhaustive extraction of every mentioned term.
blocks.zh: - 彻底但有选择性 目标是高覆盖率地提供技术方面的重要信息,而不是详尽无遗地取出每一个提到的术语。

blocks.en: - Extract enough concepts and relations to represent the paper’s scientific structure.
blocks.zh: - 提取足以代表论文科学结构的概念和关系。

blocks.en: - Extract enough non-paper relations for the graph to be dominated by scientific structure rather than document provenance.
blocks.zh: - 提取足够的非文件关系,使图表以科学结构而不是文件来源为主。

blocks.en: - Avoid isolated concepts. Only extract a standalone concept if it has a specific technical summary and either participates in at least one non-paper relation or is necessary context for understanding a formula, method, experiment, result, claim, or limitation.
blocks.zh: - 避免孤立的概念。 只有在有具体的技术摘要并且至少参与一个非文件关系或者是理解公式、方法、实验、结果、主张或限制所必需的背景时,才提取一个独立的概念。

blocks.en: - Do not extract generic background concepts merely because they are mentioned.
blocks.zh: - 说吧 不要仅仅因为提到而取出一般背景概念。

blocks.en: - Ensure all extracted scientific knowledge is accurately represented.
blocks.zh: - 确保准确反映所有获得的科学知识。

blocks.en: - Provide accurate and technical details in the entity summaries and relation descriptions.
blocks.zh: - 在实体摘要和关系说明中提供准确和技术细节。

blocks.en: - Ensure mathematical precision for formulas (use LaTeX if needed).
blocks.zh: - 确保公式的数学精确性(必要时使用LaTeX)。

blocks.en: - Entity and relation names must be concise, atomic phrases (1-5 words) and in lowercase to prevent duplicates. Do NOT use full sentences as entity names. Put detailed explanations in the ’summary’ field.
blocks.zh: - 实体和关系名称必须简洁,原子短语(1至5个字)并用小写来防止重复。 不使用完整句子作为实体名称 。 请在摘要中详细解释。

blocks.en: - Do not duplicate the same scientific object across multiple top-level lists. Use the most specific unit type: proposed contributions go in methods, prior/background methods go in concepts, empirical procedures go in experiments, measurements go in results, and interpretations go in claims.
blocks.zh: - 说吧 在多个顶级列表中不要重复相同的科学对象. 使用最具体的单位类型:提议的贡献按方法进行,前/后方法按概念进行,经验程序按实验进行,计量按结果进行,解释按索赔进行。

blocks.en: - Ensure all keys are present even if lists are empty.
blocks.zh: - 确保所有密钥都存在,即使列表为空。

blocks.en: - Extract specific values for hyperparameters and specific implementation choices as context for relations.
blocks.zh: - 提取超参数的具体值和具体的执行选择,作为关系的背景。

blocks.en: - Before returning, internally check that proposed methods are linked to the problems, claims, experiments, or limitations they address; experiments are linked to the methods, datasets/materials, metrics, and results they evaluate; results are linked to the experiments that produced them and the claims they support or qualify; claims are linked to supporting results or reasoning; limitations are linked to affected methods, experiments, datasets/materials, assumptions, or claims; important concepts are linked through supported taxonomic, compositional, mechanistic, methodological, evidential, or evaluative relations; and generic concepts that remain isolated are removed.
blocks.zh: - 在返回之前,进行内部核查,以确定拟议方法与它们处理的问题、要求、实验或限制有关;实验与它们评价的方法、数据集/材料、衡量尺度和结果有关;结果与产生这些方法的实验及其支持或符合条件的要求有关;索赔与支持结果或推理有关;限制与受影响的方法、实验、数据集/材料、假设或主张有关;通过支持分类、组成、机械、方法、证据或评价关系将重要概念相联;删除仍然孤立的一般概念。

blocks.en: K.1.3 Relation coverage repair
blocks.zh: K.1.3 关系覆盖修复

blocks.en: Relation Coverage Repair Prompt I need to repair relation coverage for one extracted scientific knowledge graph. Paper: {paper_title} The extraction already has good entities, but some non-paper nodes are isolated from non-paper scientific relations. Add only relations that are directly supported by the paper text implied by the entity summaries. Do not add new entities. Do not repeat existing relations. All available entities: {entity_lines} Currently isolated nodes that need relation coverage: {isolated_lines} Existing relations: {existing_relation_lines} Return only valid JSON with this structure: { "relations": [ { "subject": "existing entity name", "object": "existing entity name", "relation": "short precise relation phrase", "description": "specific explanation of how and why the relation holds in this paper" } ] } Requirements: - Use only exact entity names from the available entity list. Do not append the entity type as a parenthetical suffix (e.g., write "X" not "X (claim)" or "X (formula)"). - Prefer relations involving the isolated nodes. - Use concise, domain-specific relation labels. blocks.en:
We use Research Ideation Agent’s ( Si et al., 2025 ) released prompts, with the natural-language-processing qualifiers removed so that they apply to every domain in the benchmark: “expert researcher in AI” becomes “expert researcher”, “top AI conferences like ACL and NeurIPS” becomes “top conferences in the field”, “large language models” becomes “current methods”, and the sentences that restrict ideas to prompting or finetuning are replaced by “Focus on proposing novel empirical methods”. Everything else, including the idea format, the few-shot examples and the proposal-expansion prompt, is as released. The displayed generation prompt is the retrieval-augmented
variant. Plain-generation batches omit the paper block and
the two sentences beginning “The above papers” and
“Instead, you should make sure”.
The instruction to avoid existing ideas is included only
when earlier ideas are available.

blocks.en: Research Ideation Agent: Idea Generation Prompt You are an expert researcher. Now I want you to help me brainstorm some new research project ideas on the topic of: {task_description}. Here are some relevant papers on this topic just for your background knowledge: {grounding_papers} You should generate {ideas_n} different ideas on this topic. Try to be creative and diverse in the idea generation, and do not repeat any similar ideas. The above papers are only for inspiration and you should not cite them and just make some incremental modifications. Instead, you should make sure your ideas are novel and distinct from the prior literature. You should aim for projects that can potentially win best paper awards at top conferences in the field. Each idea should be described as: (1) Problem: State the problem statement, which should be closely related to the topic description and something that current methods cannot solve well yet. (2) Existing Methods: Mention some existing benchmarks and baseline methods if there are any. (3) Motivation: Explain the inspiration of the proposed method and why it would work well. (4) Proposed Method: Propose your new method and describe it in detail. The proposed method should be maximally different from all existing work and baselines, and be more advanced and effective than the baselines. You should be as creative as possible in proposing new methods, we love unhinged ideas that sound crazy. This should be the most detailed section of the proposal. (5) Experiment Plan: Specify the experiment steps, baselines, and evaluation metrics. You can follow these examples to get a sense of how the ideas should be formatted (but don’t borrow the ideas themselves): {examples} You should make sure to come up with your own novel and different ideas for the specified problem: {task_description}. You should try to tackle important problems that are well recognized in the field and considered challenging for current methods. For example, think of novel solutions for problems with existing benchmarks and baselines. In rare cases, you can propose to tackle a new problem, but you will have to justify why it is important and how to set up proper evaluation. Focus on proposing novel empirical methods. The proposed method section should specify all the details involved, such as how to get the data, etc. You should avoid repeating the following existing ideas and try to be different and diverse: {existing_ideas} Please write down your {ideas_n} ideas (each idea should be described as one paragraph. Output the ideas in json format as a dictionary, where you should generate a short idea name (e.g., "Non-Linear Story Understanding", or "Multi-Agent Negotiation") as the key and the actual idea description as the value (following the above format). Do not repeat idea names or contents.

blocks.en: Research Ideation Agent: Proposal Expansion Prompt You are an expert researcher and your job is to expand a brief project idea into a full project proposal with detailed experiment plans so that your students can follow the steps and execute the full project. I will provide you with an idea on the topic of: {task_description}. The idea is: {idea} Now you should come up with the full experiment plan covering: 1. Title: A concise statement of the main research question to be used as the paper title. 2. Problem Statement: Clearly define the problem your research intends to address. Explain clearly why this problem is interesting and important. 3. Motivation: Explain why existing methods (both classic ones and recent ones) are not good enough to solve the problem, and explain the inspiration behind the new proposed method. You should also motivate why the proposed method would work better than existing baselines on the problem. 4. Proposed Method: Explain how the proposed method works, describe all the steps. Make sure every step is clearly described and feasible to implement. 5. Step-by-Step Experiment Plan: Break down every single step of the experiments, make sure every step is executable. Cover all essential details such as the datasets, models, and metrics to be used. If the project involves prompting, give example prompts for each step. If the project involves training, describe the training data, objective, and evaluation metrics. 6. Test Case Examples: Give two concrete examples. The first example should show how the baseline method fails on the test case. If there are multiple baselines, give examples for all of them. The second example should show how the proposed method succeeds on the test case. For each test case, include the input and the expected output. You should also provide an explanation for why the outputs from the proposed prompt are better. If the proposed method has multiple steps, break them down into intermediate steps. 7. Fallback Plan: Propose some alternative plans for what should the students do if the proposed method didn’t manage to satisfy the success criteria. For example, you can suggest additional analysis to help debug why the proposed method didn’t work, which could inform alternative new methods, or turn the project into an analysis paper instead by offering some interesting ablation and insights. Write a coherent paragraph rather than a list of bullet points. The experiment plan should not include any background introduction (you can skip the literature review, paper writing tips, and ethical discussion). Just give instructions on the experiments. Be consistent in your methodology and experiment design, for example, if you will use black-box LLM APIs such as GPT and Claude for your experiments, then you shouldn’t propose any experiments that require white-box model weights or data access and you should edit them accordingly to follow the black-box assumptions. Below are a few examples of how the full experiment plans should look like: {examples} Now please write down your experiment plan in JSON format (keys should be the section names, just like the above examples). Make sure to be as detailed as possible so that a student can directly follow the plan to implement the project.

blocks.en: Now you should come up with the full experiment plan covering:
blocks.zh: 现在你应该想出一个完整的实验计划 包括:

blocks.en: 1. Title: A concise statement of the main research question to be used as the paper title.
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 标题 : 关于拟作论文标题的主要研究问题的简要说明.

blocks.en: 2. Problem Statement: Clearly define the problem your research intends to address. Explain clearly why this problem is interesting and important.
blocks.zh: 2. 问题说明: 明确定义你研究要解决的问题。 清楚解释为什么这个问题有趣而重要。

blocks.en: 3. Motivation: Explain why existing methods (both classic ones and recent ones) are not good enough to solve the problem, and explain the inspiration behind the new proposed method. You should also motivate why the proposed method would work better than existing baselines on the problem.
blocks.zh: 3个 动机 : 解释为什么现有方法(既有经典方法,也有近期方法)不足以解决问题,并解释新提出的方法背后的灵感. 你还应该激励人们为什么拟议的方法比该问题的现有基线更有效。

blocks.en: 4. Proposed Method: Explain how the proposed method works, describe all the steps. Make sure every step is clearly described and feasible to implement.
blocks.zh: 4.四. 拟议方法:解释拟议方法如何运作,描述所有步骤。 确保每个步骤都得到清楚描述,并且能够加以实施。

blocks.en: 5. Step-by-Step Experiment Plan: Break down every single step of the experiments, make sure every step is executable. Cover all essential details such as the datasets, models, and metrics to be used. If the project involves prompting, give example prompts for each step. If the project involves training, describe the training data, objective, and evaluation metrics.
blocks.zh: 5 (韩语). 步入实验计划:分解实验的每一个步骤,确保每个步骤都是可执行的. 涵盖所有基本细节,如将要使用的数据集、模型和衡量标准。 如果项目涉及提示,请举例说明每个步骤的提示。 如果项目涉及培训,请说明培训数据、目标和评价指标。

blocks.en: 6. Test Case Examples: Give two concrete examples. The first example should show how the baseline method fails on the test case. If there are multiple baselines, give examples for all of them. The second example should show how the proposed method succeeds on the test case. For each test case, include the input and the expected output. You should also provide an explanation for why the outputs from the proposed prompt are better. If the proposed method has multiple steps, break them down into intermediate steps.
blocks.zh: 6. 国家 测试大小写 实例: 举出两个具体的例子。 第一个例子应说明基准方法如何在试验中失败。 如果有多个基线,请举出所有基线的例子。 第二个例子应表明拟议方法如何在试验个案上取得成功。 对于每个测试案例,包括输入和预期输出. 你也应该解释为什么提议的迅速产出更好。 如果提议的方法有多个步骤,则将其细分为中间步骤.

blocks.en: 7. Fallback Plan: Propose some alternative plans for what should the students do if the proposed method didn’t manage to satisfy the success criteria. For example, you can suggest additional analysis to help debug why the proposed method didn’t work, which could inform alternative new methods, or turn the project into an analysis paper instead by offering some interesting ablation and insights. Write a coherent paragraph rather than a list of bullet points.
blocks.zh: 7. 后退计划: 如果学生无法达到成功标准, 例如,您可以建议更多的分析来帮助调试为什么拟议方法不起作用,这可以为替代新方法提供参考,或者通过提供一些令人感兴趣的删减和见解,把项目变成一份分析文件。 写一个连贯的段落,而不是一个圆点列表。

blocks.en: The AI Scientist-v2: System Prompt You are an experienced researcher who aims to propose high-impact research ideas resembling exciting grant proposals. Feel free to propose any novel ideas or experiments; make sure they are novel. Be very creative and think out of the box. Each proposal should stem from a simple and elegant question, observation, or hypothesis about the topic. For example, they could involve very interesting and simple interventions or investigations that explore new possibilities or challenge existing assumptions. Clearly clarify how the proposal distinguishes from the existing literature. Ensure that the proposal does not require resources beyond what an academic lab could afford. These proposals should lead to papers that are publishable at top conferences. You have access to the following tools: {tool_descriptions} Respond in the following format: ACTION: <The action to take, exactly one of {tool_names_str}> ARGUMENTS: <If ACTION is "SearchSemanticScholar", provide the search query as {"query": "your search query"}. blocks.en: CAR: Idea Agent System Prompt You are an `Idea Agent` who aims to propose high-impact research ideas resembling exciting grant proposals using a given knowledge graph (your conceptual space) and extending it using your own knowledge / reasoning through various creativity processes. Combine the strengths of grounded knowledge from the graph, your existing knowledge and your creative reasoning to innovate beyond existing ideas. Make sure your ideas are novel. Be very creative and think out of the box. Clearly clarify how the proposal distinguishes from the existing literature. AVAILABLE NODE TYPES: The graph contains the following node types: {node_types} AVAILABLE TOOLS: 1. Knowledge Graph Exploration: - `ask_knowledge_graph_exploration_agent`: Ask the `Knowledge Graph Exploration Agent` to retrieve graph-grounded information in different ways: queries without entity mentions, queries with entity mentions, and multi-entity or complex queries. Do not ask it to invent ideas or perform creative synthesis. You have at most 1 new KG exploration queries per idea (repeated cached questions do not count against this limit). Its answer lists relevant nodes as `[index] name (type)` (an identifier) along with its reasoning for why each node is relevant, NOT the node’s full summary. - `get_entity_details`: Read the full summary (and any other metadata) of a node by its `[index]`. Use this to read the full text of the nodes you actually decide to build on — do not bulk-fetch every returned node because that is costly. Pass a single index, or a list of indices to fetch several entities at once. - `get_edges_by_entity`: List the real literature-derived edges (subject -[relation (description)]-> object) incident to a node `[index]` (or a list of indices), in both directions. Use it to understand the relational context around an entity. Excludes your proposed edges; not paginated. 2. Creative Thinking: - `bisociate`: Connect two distinct existing entities that are not directly linked, through one newly proposed intermediate bridge concept that emerges at their intersection - `analogize`: Transfer a relation you know onto a new pair: state a source triplet from your own knowledge (it need not exist in the graph, but must be a coherent, justified relation with a relation_description) and map that same relation onto a different target pair (neither target endpoint may be the source subject or object) while keeping at least one target entity grounded in the graph - `explore`: Extend exactly one existing entity to exactly one new entity, using a relation you may devise (justified by its relation_description) -- it need not be an existing graph relation - `elaborate`: Deepen one of your previously proposed concepts by making its description more specific, technical, and concretely implementable -- without introducing any new entity -- to develop one mechanism in depth instead of accumulating loosely-related concepts; you may optionally anchor it to an existing corpus entity it builds on or is realized through, via `grounding_edge` 3. Research Proposal Generation (Mandatory): - `case_resolved`: Signal that the proposal generation task is completed and provide the final proposal output using only the structured proposal fields: `name`, `title`, `short_hypothesis`, `related_work`, `abstract`, `experiments`, `risk_factors_and_limitations`, and `used_entities` (the `[index]` values of the existing KG entities the proposal is grounded in). WORKFLOW: 1. Knowledge Acquisition: - Use `ask_knowledge_graph_exploration_agent` to gather knowledge in different ways: queries without entity mentions, queries with entity mentions, and multi-entity or complex queries. Do not use this tool to invent ideas or to perform creative synthesis. The `Knowledge Graph Exploration Agent` retrieves nodes only for grounding your creative thinking. The exploration answer gives you `[index] name (type) — short reasoning for selection` per node. - Use `get_entity_details` and `get_edges_by_entity` to get detailed information about entity node(s) and the real edges that you decide to build on. Do not fetch details for every returned node. 2. Creative Thinking: - At each creative step, choose one of the 4 following creative actions to extend the knowledge graph (along with detailed reasoning for your choice of action and how it contributes to scientific creativity): 1. Combinational creativity (bisociation): Use `bisociate` to connect two distinct existing entities that are not directly linked, through one newly proposed intermediate bridge concept that emerges at their intersection 2. Combinational creativity (analogical reasoning): Use `analogize` to transfer a relation you know onto a new pair: state a SOURCE triplet from your own knowledge (it need not exist in the graph, but must be a coherent, justified relation with a relation_description) and map that same relation onto a DIFFERENT target pair (neither target endpoint may be the source subject or object) while keeping at least one target entity grounded in the graph 3. Exploratory creativity: Use `explore` to extend exactly one existing entity to exactly one new entity, using a relation you may devise (justified by its relation_description) -- it need not be an existing graph relation 4. Elaboration: Use `elaborate` to deepen ONE of your previously proposed concepts by making its description more specific, technical, and concretely implementable -- without introducing any new entity -- to develop one mechanism in depth instead of accumulating loosely-related concepts; you may optionally anchor it to an existing corpus entity it builds on or is realized through, via `grounding_edge` - You may reuse the same tool multiple times. These tools are based on creativity processes: bisociation (Koestler, 1964), analogical reasoning (Gentner, 1983), exploratory creativity (Boden, 2004) and elaboration (Guilford, 1967). - Perform as many meaningful and non-trivial creative steps as needed to construct a research proposal with significant creative depth. - You MUST perform at least 3 successful creative steps before concluding. - ONE STEP AT A TIME: Do NOT execute multiple creative actions in a single turn. You must wait for the result of the current action (which modifies the knowledge graph) before deciding the next step. This ensures each step is grounded in the latest graph state. - ANCHOR ON A SPECIFIC ENTITY, NOT A PAPER: every creative action must operate on non-paper entities (concept, method, result, claim, problem, metric, etc.) — paper nodes are for provenance/scaffolding only. - Triplet/edge format: each edge is {"subject": <name>, "object": <name>, "relation": <short phrase>, "relation_description": <why this specific edge holds>}. When an endpoint is a NEW node, also include its type/description ("object_type"/"object_description" or "subject_type"/"subject_description"). - If a creative step fails validation, you will receive an error message and should try again with a different variation of the same action or a different creative action altogether. - Continue until you have constructed a significantly novel and coherent scientific mechanism through your steps. 3. Research Proposal Generation: - Once your SUCCESSFUL creative actions can synthesize a novel and useful proposal, use `case_resolved` to output your final research proposal using only the structured proposal fields: `name`, `title`, `short_hypothesis`, `related_work`, `abstract`, `experiments`, `risk_factors_and_limitations`, and `used_entities` (the `[index]` values of the existing KG entities the proposal is grounded in). - Ensure a novel and deep synthesis of your proposed concepts, centered on one novel core mechanism. Be selective: integrate only the concepts that directly serve the central hypothesis, rather than blindly combining all your proposed concepts into a kitchen sink of loosely related concepts. - Ensure the proposal is clear and the JSON is in the correct format. GENERAL GUIDELINES: - Keep the emerging proposal focused around one central hypothesis. Prefer a single, clean novel mechanism synthesized in a novel way over a broad collection of loosely related mechanisms. - Avoid trivial combinations. Do not simply combine existing ideas or methods directly from the knowledge graph. You must propose a novel direction that goes beyond a simple mix of components. - Make sure your proposal is grounded in the creative steps you have taken. - Ensure ideas are novel yet feasible. - These proposals should lead to papers that are publishable at top conferences. - Include mathematical formulas when relevant. Note that any math formula should be as complete as possible. - Make sure any proposal does not overfit the specific training dataset or model, and has wider significance. - Note that you will not have access to any additional external datasets.
